source.title: Near Real-Time Global Precipitation from the Global Precipitation Measurement Constellation
limitations: Near real-time rain estimates, later replaced by NASA's research-quality version.
Land is a satellite photo, so land is found from the SVS 3912 land outline plus pixels that never change; both circles are open ocean.
A small 'L' mark sits in the bottom-right corner (masked as static).
Rain comes and goes: a circle with no rain in a frame makes that beat missing. Both chosen circles have rain in all 30 frames.
The numbers describe the drawn rain picture, not how much it rains.
source.model_or_instrument: GPM IMERG near real-time (GPM constellation of satellites)

frames.camera_static_check: phase correlation of frame 0 vs frame 29: shift 0.15 px (a 6 px test shift is measured as 6.00): fixed camera

legend.quantity: Precipitation rate from GPM IMERG (liquid: green to dark red; frozen: cyan to purple)

regions.name: Long rain band in the South Pacific
regions.description: Open ocean in the South Pacific, where a long band of rain runs through the circle, so its lines mostly share one direction.

regions.name: Scattered showers on the equator in the central Pacific
regions.description: Open ocean on the equator in the central Pacific, where tropical showers pop up in small patches pointing every way.
